extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, geologists, archaeologists, and scientifically literate public
extracted.subtask_description: Classification and description of megalithic dolmen-mounds and their interior structures in Brittany (types, examples, and remarks); also includes related geological nomenclature principles and a short editorial on principles for government support of science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral classification: callais vs turquoise
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...elle en différe sensiblement, aussi bien par les proportions de ses principes constituents que par ses caractéres. M. Damour, d’après les différences appréciables qui existent entre ces deux matiéres, les sépare dans la classification des especes. Il emprunte à pleine le nom de callais, qu'il applique à notre minéral, et réserve celui de turquoise a la pierre précieuse de couleur bleu de ciel...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline: distinguish mineral species by appreciable differences in proportions of constituent principles and by characters (physical appearance); use distinct names when differences are significant (example: callais applied to one mineral, turquoise reserved for sky-blue gem used in jewelry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 1 — Long barrow (interior structure: Nil)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long barrow. Interior structure: Nil. Example: Kerlescant (?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Comparatively rare; presence of an erect menhir noted in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 2 — Round ditto; Simple kist (C.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Round ditto. Simple kist. Example: Carnoet, Finistere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Frequent. In the two examples given, bronze implements were found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 3 — Ordinary megalithic dolmen with single chamber and narrow entrance passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary megalithic dolmen, consisting of single chamber, with narrow entrance passage. Labeled 'C.' in table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: This is the commonest type of tumulus and forms the basis for many variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 4 — Many-chambered megalithic dolmen (single narrow entrance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many-chambered megalithic dolmen, consisting of several chambers with a single narrow entrance. (C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Keriaval. Noted as a frequent variation of the single-chamber type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 5 — Many-chambered dolmen with dry-walling and vaulted chambers
rubrics_metrics.description: Many-chambered dolmen, chambers of dry walling, and vaulted; narrow entrance, megalithic and ceiled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 6 — Long, narrow, megalithic chamber (sometimes divided), sometimes with dolmen entrance (Long ditto)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long ditto. Long, narrow, megalithic chamber, sometimes divided, sometimes with dolmen entrance. (C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Garren-dol. Notes: There is a peristalith at Kerlescant; some examples have tolmen entrances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 7 — Megalithic dolmen with passage at a sharp angle to chamber
rubrics_metrics.description: Round ditto. Megalithic dolmen, with passage at a sharp angle with chamber. (C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: A rare example; the entrance passage descends into the chamber and was found divided by walls of loose masonry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 8 — Megalithic dolmen with curved gallery or passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ditto ditto. Megalithic dolmen, with curved gallery or passage. (C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Le Rocher. Remarks: Le Rocher is yet covered with its tumulus and is a unique and perfect specimen; the type of ornamentation (Pierres Plates) is similar though denuded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 9 — Two or more megalithic dolmens either parallel or at right angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Ditto ditto. Two or more megalithic dolmens, either parallel, or at right angles to one another. (C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Grottes de Kerozille. Remarks: At Kerozille the centre dolmens are at right angles to the others; in other instances the dolmens are parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 10 — Square megalithic chamber with long straight avenue and elaborate ornamentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ditto ditto. Square megalithic chamber, and a long straight avenue, with elaborate ornamentation. (C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Gavr' Inis. Remarks: The most elaborately decorated dolmen known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 11 — Long megalithic tumulus with additional smaller kists, vaulted structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Long ditto. Megalithic dolmen at one extremity, and also other smaller kists, ceiled and vaulted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Manné-Lud; Le Moustoir. Remarks: In Manné-Lud, besides the large dolmen, is a vaulted kist and curious arrangement of stones; in Le Moustoir a dolmen and three other partially megalithic and partially vaulted structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type 12 — Immense tumuli partly megalithic, partly ceiled or vaulted, elliptical or conical
rubrics_metrics.description: Immense tumuli, more or less partly megalithic, partly ceiled, and partly vaulted; more or less elliptical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/Remarks: Comparatively insignificant kists; Tumiac is conical with inhumation relics; Manné-ér-H’Roék is longer and more truncated and contained no human relics; Mont St. Michel long and narrow mound showed signs of incineration of human remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of fossils and stratigraphical relations to define geological formations (nomenclature principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘...establishing on stratigraphical and palæontological grounds a succession and a geological nomenclature.’ Formations are characterised by peculiar fossils and traced regionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Name and subdivide rock series based on stratigraphical sections and palaeontological evidence (fossil content), and trace formations regionally; historical practice: Murchison named Silurian after the Silures, Sedgwick proposed Cambrian, divisions (Upper/Middle/Lower) were made based on fossil presence and rock characters (e.g., Bala limestone, Llanberis slates, Harlech grits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle for government intervention in support of science
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘If a certain course of procedure be for the obvious benefit of the whole people, and if its accomplishment be beyond the power of private associations, but not beyond that of Government, then surely it ought to be undertaken.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied test for public action: intervene when (1) project benefits the whole people, (2) private associations cannot accomplish it, and (3) government has the capacity. Examples: steam packets and food supply may be left to private enterprise; import inspection of diseased cattle and maintenance of meteorological observatories are proper government actions; some scientific infrastructure (Kew Observatory, sun observations) struggled under private funds and argue for public support.
